title: AI Act Scientific Panel
summary: The AI Act Scientific Panel is a group of experts that examines and advises on the proposed AI regulations. They use the latest research to make sure the rules support innovation while protecting safety and ethical standards.

summary: This document outlines a proposal to create standardized guidelines for the development, deployment, and governance of AI systems, aiming to ensure consistency and reliability across different organizations. It presents the steps, criteria, and benefits of adopting a unified standard, emphasizing the importance of transparency, safety, and interoperability in AI technologies.

summary: This document gives a visual overview of the iterative drafting process used by a community of practice, showing how ideas are refined through repeated cycles. It illustrates the stages of drafting, review, feedback, and revision that guide collaborative policy development.

title: Code of Practice: 1st Draft
summary: This draft Code of Practice establishes foundational standards for designing, deploying, and governing artificial intelligence systems, emphasizing transparency, accountability, and safety. It seeks to guide stakeholders in ensuring AI is developed and used responsibly while protecting users and society.

title: Code of Practice: 2nd Draft
summary: The “Code of Practice: 2nd Draft” is a set of guidelines designed to help organizations develop, deploy, and manage AI systems responsibly, covering areas such as fairness, transparency, and user safety. It outlines best practices, risk‑management steps, and accountability measures that companies should follow to comply with emerging AI standards.

title: Code of Practice: 3rd Draft
summary: The document sets out a set of guidelines and standards for responsible AI development and use. As the third draft of the code of practice, it aims to clarify roles, responsibilities, and best practices for organizations and practitioners.

title: AI Pact Draft
summary: The AI Pact Draft is a proposed agreement that aims to set clear rules for creating and using artificial intelligence responsibly. It highlights key principles such as safety, fairness, transparency, and accountability to make sure AI benefits everyone and operates safely.

title: AI Pact Final
summary: The AI Pact Final is an international agreement that brings together governments, industry, and civil society to set common principles for the safe and responsible development and use of artificial intelligence. It outlines commitments to transparency, accountability, human rights protection, and cooperation on research, regulation, and global standards to ensure AI benefits all while mitigating risks.

title: Guidelines on prohibited artificial intelligence (AI) practices
summary: This policy lists the AI activities that are disallowed, such as deceptive manipulation, autonomous lethal weapon use, or exploitation of personal data. Its goal is to prevent harm and promote responsible use of AI by banning these prohibited practices.

title: Guidelines on AI System Definition
summary: The document outlines criteria for defining what constitutes an AI system, including technical capabilities, use cases, and governance considerations. It provides guidance for organizations to classify and manage AI systems consistently across projects.

title: Communication on Boosting Start-Ups & Innovation
summary: This policy outlines strategies for improving communication to support the growth of start‑ups and spur innovation. It emphasizes best practices, collaborative frameworks, and resource allocation that enable new businesses to thrive and bring innovative ideas to market.

title: EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups
summary: The EuroHPC Initiative for Start-Ups is a program designed to help early‑stage technology companies gain access to high‑performance computing resources. By providing training, funding, and infrastructure support, it aims to accelerate innovation and bring new HPC‑driven products to the European market.

title: Slideshow: Webinar on Risk Management
